ask.text:
(drummer) has spent the whole dry season hollowing out a great log for a new drum, and tonight it will be played for the first time. The elders say a new drum has to be woken properly, or it sulks forever: someone who has never danced must dance to its first beat.
Everyone looks at (subject). (subject) has never danced in (subject.his/her) life. Not at weddings, not at festivals, not once. (subject.He/She) would rather swim to the next island. Should (subject) dance, or refuse and let someone else try?

c1o1.text: (subject) dances badly, wildly, and without stopping, until the drum and (subject) are both exhausted. Everyone agrees it is the worst dancing they have ever seen and the best first beat a drum has ever had. From then on (subject) dances at every festival, still badly, still with complete joy.

c1o2.text: On the third beat, (subject) jumps, lands on the side of (subject.his/her) foot, and goes down with a crack everyone hears over the drum. The ankle never heals straight, and (subject) walks with a hitch from then on. The drum, the elders say, is properly woken. (subject) says, with feeling, that the drum can go back to sleep.

c1.text: (drummer) raises the sticks. BOOM. The sound goes through (subject)'s feet and up (subject.his/her) legs, and before (subject.he/she) can think about it, (subject.his/her) feet are moving...

c2o1.text: The eldest villager in the village, (eldest), who has also never danced, gets up slowly and says (subject.he/she) supposes it's (subject.his/her) turn. (subject.He/She) dances one slow, careful circle around the drum. Everyone cries. In the firelight, (subject.his/her) face looks years younger, and in the morning, it still does. The drum sounds wonderful ever after.

c2o2.text: Nobody else will do it. The drum is played anyway, and it sounds flat and dull, like hitting a wet log. (drummer) tries for weeks to make it sing, and fails, and by the end of the season has lost (subject.his/her) love of drumming altogether. The great drum ends up as a water trough for the pigs.

c2.text: "No," says (subject). "Get someone else." The crowd groans. (drummer) shrugs and looks for another first-time dancer...
